verses.text: At that time the LORD said to me, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Also make a wooden chest.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. Then you must put them in the chest."
So I made a chest out of acacia wood and cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Then I went up the mountain carrying the two tablets in my hands.

The LORD wrote on these tablets what he had written before: the Ten Commandments he had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire, on the day you were all gathered there. Then the LORD gave them to me.
I turned and came down the mountain and put the tablets in the chest I had made. They are still there, just as the LORD commanded me.
(The Israelites travelled from the wells of the people of Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
From there they travelled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the Ark of the LORD's Covenant, to stand before the LORD to serve him, and to give blessings in his name. They still do this today.
That is why the Levites have no share of land among the other tribes. The LORD himself is their share, as the LORD your God told them.)
I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I did the first time, and once again the LORD listened to me. He chose not to destroy you.
The LORD said to me, "Get up and lead the people on their journey, so that they may go in and take over the land I promised their ancestors I would give them."

And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? He asks you to fear the LORD your God, to live the way he wants, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul,
and to obey the LORD's commands and rules that I am giving you today for your own good.
Look, the heavens, even the highest heavens, belong to the LORD your God, and so does the earth and everything in it.
Yet the LORD loved your ancestors and took delight in them. He chose you, their descendants, above all other peoples, as you can see today.
So change your hearts and stop being stubborn.
For the LORD your God is God over all gods and Lord over all lords. He is the great God, mighty and awesome. He does not take sides, and he does not accept bribes.
He makes sure orphans and widows are treated fairly. He loves the foreigners living among you and gives them food and clothing.
So you too must love foreigners, because you yourselves were foreigners in Egypt.
Fear the LORD your God and serve him. Hold tightly to him, and make your promises only in his name.
He is the one you should praise. He is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things that you have seen with your own eyes.
When your ancestors went down to Egypt, there were only seventy of them. But now the LORD your God has made you as many as the stars in the sky.
